A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the gut mesothelial cells of the sea cucumber can be viewed as a reservoir of multipotent stem-like cells, whose fate is determined by complex interactions between the developmental/cancer-related regulatory pathways.
the gut mesothelioma of H.glaberrima is a highly dynamic tissue with a unique ability to switch from one phenotype to another.
the gut mesothelial cells in sea cucumber are a highly dynamic cell population, capable of rapid proliferation in response to injury and of undergoing dramatic changes in their gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gut mesothelial cells are capable of switching their gene expression patterns and cell behavior to accommodate different developmental programs, depending on the needs of the organism.

the sea cucumber digestive tube is a good model for studying the interplay of the genes that are known to be involved both in embryogenesis and in tumor growth, and for investigating the role of these genes in tissue regeneration.

the gut mesothelial cells of sea cucumber, which are the main cell type responsible for regeneration of the digestive tube, have the potential to undergo a transition similar to the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) that is observed in tumor progression.
